molecules.title: Molecules: Mena-LAM-s (lam5-v1)
molecules.body: Molecules run on Mena-LAM-s by default (35 MB, loads in about 60 ms). Besides energies and forces it predicts partial charges, the dipole and the polarizability, which give IR & Raman spectra, and includes D3(BJ) dispersion. Fused GPU kernels and a low-memory CPU mode run biomolecules of thousands of atoms on a laptop.

materials.title: Periodic materials: Mena-LAM-preview (lam-400k)
materials.body: Crystals and surfaces use Mena-LAM-preview (lam-400k) by default: Matbench Discovery F1 0.905, CPS 0.849, DynaMat MD CMDS 0.787. Mena-LAM-s can also be chosen for crystals in Settings; on an Apple M3 Max laptop it runs 44,670 atoms/s at 8,192 silicon atoms and fits 65,536 atoms in 5.80 GB.

plf547.title: PLF547 protein–ligand interaction error vs. CCSD(T)
plf547.note: Lower is better. Mena-LAM-s combines learned partial charges, damped Coulomb and C6 dispersion.
plf547.source: PLF547 benchmark (547 protein–ligand complexes vs. gold-standard CCSD(T)).

tier2_scaling.title: Molecular scaling on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB): fused GPU kernels vs. plain PyTorch
tier2_scaling.note: The fused path runs message passing, exact Coulomb and D3 dispersion as Metal GPU kernels with constant extra memory. At 8,192 atoms plain PyTorch runs out of memory (>38.1 GB), while the fused path runs at 11,727 atoms/s in 4.89 GB (2.22 GB in low-memory mode).
tier2_scaling.source: Measured on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB).

cpu_and_workflows.title: CPU low-memory mode (0.16 MB/atom) and batched GPU workflows

facts.CPU drug single-point: 17.1–39.2 ms (~15–45 ms: H₂O 17.1 ms, caffeine 29.4 ms, ibuprofen 39.2 ms)
facts.GPU eval_batch (64× drugs, N=18–92): 329.4 structs/s on M3 Max GPU (4.44× faster than plain PyTorch, 74.3)
facts.GPU eval_batch (32× pockets, N=200–310): 64.3 structs/s in 0.74 GB (6.77× faster, 4.9× lower RAM)
facts.GPU relax_batch (24× L-BFGS, 35 steps): 2.45 s = 9.80 relax/s (30.05× faster than 73.60 s serial ASE)
facts.Caffeine Hessian + IR + Raman: 0.508 s for 144 displacements (3.53 ms/disp, 10.86× faster than 5.52 s CPU serial)
facts.FAIRChem OMol25 full runs on M3 Max: GEOM Conformers (8,245 relax) in 29.3 min (beats Cloud A100 31.2 min); Ligand Strain in 38.1 min (vs. 49.0 min A100)

cpu_and_workflows.source: Measured on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB).

accuracy_and_spectroscopy.title: Molecular accuracy, electrostatics & spectroscopy highlights (Mena-LAM-s)

facts.TorsionNet500 (DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS): 0.205 kcal/mol barrier MAE (R² = 0.9802; 12,000 pts in 10.8 s = 1,111 structs/s)
facts.Wiggle150 strained conformers: 1.066 kcal/mol MAE (R² = 0.9971; ahead of ωB97M-D3BJ/QZVP 1.18 & AIMNet2 2.35)
facts.OMol25 S2EF val_sub5k & Biomolecules: 1.640 kcal/mol E / 0.340 kcal/mol/Å F; Val-Comp Biomolecules 53.87 meV (UMA-M-1.1: 58.65)
facts.Dipole & polarizability (def2-TZVPD): Neutral dipole r = 0.9997 (MAE 0.009 e·Å); α_iso scaling r = 0.9955; Raman anisotropy γ r = 0.967
facts.QVib 1,366 conformers & IR spectra: Freq MAE 5.58 cm⁻¹ vs. PBE0+MBD (4.43 vs. ωB97M-V); IR cosine 0.8761 (matches MACE-POLAR-1 0.8765); Born charges r = 0.9993

accuracy_and_spectroscopy.source: PLF547, TorsionNet500, Folmsbee, Wiggle150, GMTKN55, OMol25 validation and QVib benchmarks.

hardware_banner.title: A100 & Apple M3 Max laptop vs. H100 / H200 / Blackwell / H20 data-center GPUs
hardware_banner.dynamat: On the official Matbench Discovery DynaMat v1.0 MD benchmark, Mena-LAM-preview ran on 1× NVIDIA A100 (40 GB, 1.56 TB/s bandwidth) at 24.7 atoms/ms (2.37 h total), while 44 of 45 competing models ran on newer H100, H200, or RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs (38 on H200 at 4.80 TB/s, 3 on H100 at 3.35 TB/s, 3 on Blackwell 96 GB). Despite running on A100, Mena-LAM-preview finished in 2.37 h (ORB v2 MPA on H200: 2.61 h; DPA-4.1-Air-OAM: 3.52 h) with 0.72 GB peak memory (DPA-4.1-Air-OAM: 1.33 GB; DPA-4.1-Max-OAM-PFT: 22.3 GB) and CMDS 0.787.
hardware_banner.diamond: On memory per atom (0.66 MB/atom on A100, 0.82 MB/atom on M3 Max, 0.33 MB/atom in low-memory mode), Mena-LAM-preview uses 8×–22× less memory than Meta's UMA-S 1.2.1 Nitro (6.5–9.5 MB/atom standard, ~18.5 MB/atom on 158-nbr diamond, hard-capped at 15,000 atoms on H200) and 9.5× less than DPA-4.1-Air-OAM (7.79 MB/atom on diamond). Even on an Apple M3 Max laptop (36 GB, 300 GB/s — 13.3× lower bandwidth than H20), Mena-LAM-preview reaches 14,480 atoms/s (14.48 atoms/ms) on 158-nbr/atom diamond and 21,700 atoms/s on CsSnI₃.
